fi-sparisoma-viride.title: Stoplight Parrotfish
fi-sparisoma-viride.summary: A Caribbean parrotfish; big terminal-phase males are green with a yellow spot on the tail (the "stoplight"). Juveniles are shy and hide among rock or seagrass. It grows large and grazes algae by day with a beak-like jaw, sleeping on the bottom at night.
rows: About 18 in (Saltwaterfish.com adult size); wild record 64 cm (25.2 in) TL (FishBase)
Mostly algae in the wild; offer marine algae and a varied diet with vitamins
Western Atlantic: southern Florida (USA), Bermuda, Bahamas, and throughout the Caribbean Sea to Brazil
notes: Needs a lot of swimming room.
warn: Expert-only fish: it grazes on corals and invertebrates, so not for reef tanks.
